liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodleloo** (2 reviews): Jerry fumbles the lyrics but redeems it with a strong finishing jam; Reviewer recalls the Half-Step blazing, and the closing Lovelight being just as hot [10][14]
- **Looks Like Rain** (2 reviews): Reviewer says it would be hard to find a better version of this song; Reviewer calls this version stunning, with drums, keys and the whole band on fire [10][11]
- **Walkin' Blues** (1 review): Reviewer hears several moments of dynamic interplay between the guitars [20]
- **Candyman** (1 review): Reviewer finds this performance effectively somber [20]
- **Loser** (1 review): Reviewer praises the depth of feeling and sense of loss in the performance [20]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Coming out of space into Truckin', the reviewer and partner felt as if they had melted together [13]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-03-24.140261.sbd.miller.flac2496** (recommended): soundboard; 19 songs; 151 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd88-03-24.sbd.willy.15127.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 148 min; rated 4.19/5 by 25 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the tape they have is of poor quality; Reviewer finds the mix muddy and the recording disappointing; The start of Mississippi Half-Step is cut off in this recording [10][12][15][16]
- **gd1988-03-24.sbd.miller.91232.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 149 min; rated 4.1/5 by 10 [3]
- **gd1988-03-24.148853.fob.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 146 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [5]

## Around the show

- It was the reviewer's and their future wife's first psychedelic Dead show, and it made them devoted fans [13]
- The Omni has since been torn down, as the reviewer notes [14]
- Police arrested people in the parking lot after one man had a severe bad trip [18]
- A group from Oxford College of Emory attended; reviewer's first show, and they decided to follow the band afterward [19]
- Only the 6/21/84 Looks Like Rain comes close to this one, in the reviewer's experience [11]
- Looks Like Rain here is superb but falls short of the 3-30-88 version, in this reviewer's view [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-03-24.140261.sbd.miller.flac2496**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-R90) [1]. Also: Two sets of masters were combined to make this show complete [1]
- **gd88-03-24.sbd.willy.15127.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>MC>DAT>CDR (Healy Matrix)Eac(secure with proper offsets) >cool edit pro > shntool >cdwav> shn by Ernie Dodd & Willy [2]
- **gd1988-03-24.sbd.miller.91232.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (TDK SA-X90) D [3]. Also: Chain: soundboard to cassette master, cassette, DAT, CD, Samplitude, then FLAC; This source supplies all of Set 1 and a short stretch of Space, with pitch correction applied [3]
- **gd1988-03-24.148853.fob.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Michael Hessberg; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Michael Hessberg's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser ME-80 mics > Sony D5M [5]. Also: A 12-second patch in Space comes from an ultramatrix source [5]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead The Omni - March 24, 1988](https://www.dead.net/show/march-24-1988) [22]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead The Omni - March 24, 1988](https://www.dead.net/show/march-24-1988) [23]
- Poster by Robbi Cohn: [1988-03-24 The Omni, Atlanta, GA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1988-03-24-the-omni-atlanta-ga-usa/) [24]
